title: Crashing when Awake is set to Keep awake indefinitely and PC enters standby
author: louis1642
summary: Awake indefinite mode is reported to let the PC enter standby and then leave PowerToys crashed on resume, and the thread already includes a diagnostic ZIP plus a closely related Awake sleep/crash report.

judgment.rationale: The report already pins one specific Awake mode, one specific failure sequence, and includes a fresh bug-report ZIP, so the next useful step is a maintainer-side standby/resume reproduction rather than another generic evidence request.
evidence: The reporter gives a concrete two-step repro: set Awake to "Keep awake indefinitely" and wait for the PC to enter standby.
The observed failure is specific: the machine still enters standby and PowerToys has crashed after wake.
A PowerToys diagnostic ZIP is attached in the issue body.
A later related issue, #49461, reports another Awake overnight sleep/crash pattern on Windows 11 25H2, which suggests this is not obviously a one-off configuration typo.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce indefinite Awake on a Windows 11 standby/resume path, then inspect whether the failure is in sleep prevention itself, the resume-time reapply path, or the post-resume process stability path.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys fix is plausible, but the public evidence still needs a maintainer-side reproduction pass to distinguish the exact failing standby/resume path.

issue_context.summary: Awake set to keep the system awake indefinitely is reported to allow standby anyway, and when the machine wakes back up PowerToys is no longer running.
known_information: The issue is on PowerToys 0.100.2 with Windows 11 25H2 and includes a public PowerToysReport ZIP.
The selected Awake mode is explicitly "Keep awake indefinitely".
The reporter says the whole PC enters standby, not just that the display turns off.
Issue #49461 was cross-linked later as another Awake sleep/crash report, although that issue describes a different Awake state.
inferences: This looks more like a suspend/resume handling bug than a simple misunderstanding of the "Keep screen on" option.
The crash-after-wake symptom suggests that even if sleep prevention failed, there may also be a separate resume-time stability problem in the Awake process path.
issue_context.analysis: The issue is specific enough for a maintainer-side reproduction and log review. The reporter has already supplied the key mode selection and a diagnostic bundle, so asking for more generic information would add less value than reproducing the standby/resume path.
initial_investigation: src/modules/Awake/Awake/Core/Manager.cs applies indefinite Awake through SetThreadExecutionState using ES_SYSTEM_REQUIRED | ES_CONTINUOUS, with ES_DISPLAY_REQUIRED added only when display-on mode is requested.

src/modules/Awake/Awake/Core/TrayHelper.cs listens for WM_POWERBROADCAST resume and power-status events and calls Manager.ReapplyAwakeState(), so there is already explicit resume-time logic to inspect.

Manager.ReapplyAwakeState() simply queues the current execution state again; the public report does not yet reveal whether the failure happens before sleep, during resume, or after resume while reapplying state.

actions.label: Approve Awake standby/resume investigation
actions.note: The likely fix is inside Awake sleep-prevention or resume handling, but the exact failing branch still needs local reproduction.

actions.label: Reproduce Awake standby crash
actions.note: Verify whether indefinite Awake fails to block standby, crashes after resume, or both on a Windows 11 standby path.

prerequisites: Use a Windows 11 machine where sleep/standby is expected to occur normally.
Enable Awake and set the mode to "Keep awake indefinitely".
Prefer a setup close to the report if available, including Windows 11 25H2.
steps: Enable Awake indefinite mode and leave the machine idle long enough that it would normally enter standby.
Confirm whether the PC still enters standby even though Awake is active.
Wake the machine and check whether PowerToys is still running, then correlate the sleep/resume timestamps with Awake logs and any crash evidence from the attached diagnostic bundle.
reproduce.expected_result: With Awake set to keep the system awake indefinitely, the machine should not enter standby and PowerToys should still be running normally after any wake/resume event.

proposed_fixes.title: Harden Awake against the reported standby/resume failure path
proposed_fixes.root_cause: The current best fit is that Awake indefinite mode is not surviving the reporter's standby path correctly: either the keep-awake request is not preventing that sleep state, or the module is destabilized when the system resumes and re-applies state.
plan: Reproduce the exact indefinite-mode standby/resume sequence on a current build and confirm whether the first failure is unexpected sleep, a resume-time exception, or both.
Inspect the Awake power-event handling path around TrayHelper power broadcasts and Manager.ReapplyAwakeState() to see whether the module re-enters an invalid state after standby.
Fix the specific standby/resume branch that fails and add coverage for indefinite Awake surviving the same sleep/wake sequence without crashing.
verification: With indefinite Awake enabled, the machine should remain out of standby on the reproduced configuration.
If the system is forced through a wake/resume event, PowerToys should remain running and Awake should continue to report the correct mode afterward.

confidence.rationale: The module, mode, and symptom are clear, but the public thread does not yet distinguish whether the primary defect is failed sleep prevention, failed resume recovery, or a combined path.
